statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 remains far below the block threshold, while stress holds in the high band on the unresolved energy, trade and rate channels.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour: NQ has faded off its session high rather than extending from it, volatility sits near the day low, and no repeated extension after failed retracements is observed. The narrow flagged window covers the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour and closing auction, where Consumer Credit and rebalancing flow meet the widest sector dispersion of the session.
headline: NQ fades 157 points off its session high with VIX near the day low, while WTI back above $92.90 and a 4.474% three-year auction stop keep the stress channels open
body: NQ futures trade near 29,607.75, up 0.14% on the session, inside a 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 day range. Price has come 157 points off the session high while holding 183 points above the low, which places it in the middle-upper part of the range rather than at an extreme. That two-sided rotation is the direct opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure that overwhelms this strategy, so tail is held at 6. The cash index agrees: the Nasdaq-100 stands at 29,572.38, up 0.10%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 range and above the 29,544.15 prior close. Volatility remains decayed rather than merely stable, with VIX at 15.26, down 0.26%, at the low end of a 15.22 to 15.94 day range after fully unwinding the morning spike. The rates channel is firmer but orderly. The 10-year yield is at 4.796%, up about one basis point and at the top of a narrow 4.760 to 4.800 range; the 5-year is at 4.564% and the 13-week bill at 3.775%. The US 3-year note auction that fell in the 17:00 UTC hour has since printed, stopping at 4.474% against a 4.291% prior, an eighteen basis point increase in short-end funding cost that has not so far disturbed equity structure. Index internals stay sharply split, which keeps the dominant mode at mixed rather than trend-up or trend-down. Semiconductors lead on Qualcomm's multi-generational custom-silicon agreement with Amazon Web Services, which carries warrants over 25 million QCOM shares at $161.26 tied to up to $60 billion of purchase orders and lifted the stock as much as 9.5%; Intel is up around 5% on reported price increases and Oracle around 5% ahead of Thursday's earnings. Against that, the Dow is down 1.01% at 52,872.77 and the S&P 500 is down about 0.35% at 7,691.73. Rotation into a single-name silicon catalyst against broad cyclical weakness is dispersion, not index-level one-way pressure. The energy channel has firmed again since the prior assessment. WTI near $92.97 is up 1.63% and at its highest since 3 June, with Brent near $97.86 up 0.72% and still testing $100, after Saudi Arabia halted operations at several southern energy facilities following Houthi strikes. The counterweight is the reported Iran-Oman temporary Hormuz corridor, which Iran's foreign ministry says is days away and would be lodged with the International Maritime Organization, though reporting indicates transit fees remain a genuine point of disagreement. Neither the outage duration nor the corridor terms is resolved, which is why stress edges up to 69 rather than easing. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about $20 billion of US goods took effect today. Rate expectations are the third open channel: Friday's strong payrolls report has left market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve hike broadly balanced around the 50 to 66 percent range ahead of Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI, with the FOMC meeting on 15-16 September. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 16:52 UTC and is marginally past the 90-minute freshness limit at this cutoff, so it is treated as stale supporting colour only and is not relied upon; the independent live research above is the evidence base. The flagged window stays at the 19:00 to 20:00 UTC power hour and closing auction, where the Consumer Credit print and index rebalancing flow concentrate into that sector dispersion.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band without interruption. Tail ran between 5 and 10 from Monday evening through Tuesday morning, stepped up to 15 in the 14:00 UTC slot on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back to 8, 7 and 6 as that leg was fully retraced. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to a peak of 72 in early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect, and has since eased to the high 60s. The dominant mode was mixed for most of the window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, sat at normal through the quiet Monday evening hours, and turned to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens with the session high faded rather than extended, conditional tail at 6 and volatility at the day low. It steps up into the 19:00 UTC power hour and the 20:00 UTC closing auction, where Consumer Credit and index rebalancing flow meet the widest sector dispersion of the session; that pair of hours is the flagged window and carries the late-session peak of 10. Conditional tail then falls to the horizon floor of 5 through the Asian session, with the 07:00 UTC European open on 9 September and the 13:30 UTC US cash open as the next flow checkpoints. The first full hour after that open carries the horizon peak at 13, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion. The horizon closes on the 17:00 UTC pairing of the Apple product event keynote and the US 10-Year Note Auction. All 24 slots stay inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where the halted Saudi operations have no confirmed restart date while the reported Iran-Oman Hormuz corridor cuts the other way; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect; and rate expectations into Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels resolves inside the horizon, while confidence decays overnight as the live evidence base ages and recovers once the 9 September cash session provides fresh observable structure.
